science.name: Dead Science
science.test: 20 historical target-disease programmes (10 failed in Phase 2/3 for lack of efficacy, 10 approved), scored under each programme's own as_of cutoff
science.headline_metric: separation of mean risk score, failed minus approved

comparison.mann_whitney_method: two-sided normal approximation with tie correction

baseline.description: Published all-indication phase base rate of failure, assigned to every programme
baseline.source: Hay et al. 2014 (doi:10.1038/nbt.2786) / BIO-Informa-QLS 2021, Phase II->III transition
baseline.note: A constant predictor cannot rank, so its AUROC is 0.5 and its expected precision@k equals cohort prevalence. Per-therapy-area rates were not used: those figures were not verified against the source reports.

trial.name: Dead Trial
trial.test: 1350 interventional Phase 2/3 drug trials started on or after 2022-01-01 with a terminal status, ranked by similarity to 2000 trials completed strictly before 2022-01-01
trial.headline_metric: precision@20 of the graveyard-similarity ranking, post-2022 test cohort

phase_base_rate.description: Graveyard termination base rate assigned to every test trial
phase_base_rate.note: A constant predictor cannot rank, so AUROC is 0.5 and expected precision@k equals test-cohort prevalence.

size_only.note: Unavailable on this cohort: every test trial has finished, so all of them report ACTUAL rather than ESTIMATED enrollment. Ranking on actual enrollment would read the outcome, since a terminated trial stops small, so no size-only baseline can be computed here without leakage.

graveyard_cross_validation.note: Model selection used these graveyard folds only. The post-2022 test cohort was scored once, with the k chosen here.

trial.finding: The similarity model carries real signal inside the pre-2022 graveyard (cross-validated AUROC 0.7185081374321881) but does not survive the 2022-01-01 boundary (test AUROC 0.47938, precision@20 0.4 against prevalence 0.3704). Protocol shape predicts termination among trials of the same era and fails to transfer to the next one. On this evidence the trial lane must not claim to forecast termination from protocol fields alone.

enrollment_leakage_audit.why_enrollment_is_excluded: Enrollment is excluded from the model's feature allowlist. For a terminated trial the current record usually reports actual (small) enrollment, so both the count and its ESTIMATED/ACTUAL type carry outcome information.

caveats: ClinicalTrials.gov's historical-version endpoint returns 403 to unauthenticated clients, so test trials are scored from their current record, not a pre-start snapshot. The allowlist removes outcome fields but cannot prove a protocol field was never amended after start.

Trials started on or after 2022-01-01 that already have a terminal status over-represent short and early-stopped studies, because long trials are still running. The measured prevalence is reported, not assumed.
Cohorts are the earliest-registered matching trials (sort=StudyFirstPostDate:asc) up to a cap, not a random sample of the registry.

These numbers measure the reference graveyard-similarity scorer defined in this module, not the product lane in checks/trial. That lane scores an asset against its indication's trial landscape rather than predicting one trial's fate, so it cannot be evaluated by a per-trial termination benchmark and is not what this backtest reports.

market.name: Dead Market / Resistance
market.test: 7 targeted drugs with solved co-crystal structures and 14 documented clinical escape mutations; every residue ranked by exact heavy-atom contact distance to the bound drug plus UniProt variant density
market.headline_metric: recall@10 of known clinical escapes (micro-average over escapes)
market.baseline_metric: expected recall@10 of random selection within the binding pocket

random_whole_chain.description: Uniform random residue selection across the resolved chain

random_in_pocket.description: Uniform random selection among residues under 8.0 A of the drug; this baseline is already told where the pocket is

scoring.note: Weights are chosen heuristics, not fitted to the labels.

cases.note: C797S removes the cysteine osimertinib covalently binds
T790M is the classic gatekeeper escape from first-generation EGFR inhibitors
ABL1 numbering in 2HYY follows the 1a isoform; offset verified live
C481S removes the cysteine ibrutinib covalently binds

excluded_cases.reason: no established BRAF kinase-domain escape point mutations to recall
excluded_cases.note: Clinical vemurafenib resistance is driven by NRAS/MEK1 mutations, BRAF splice variants and amplification rather than by kinase-domain point mutations

caveats: Contact distance can only find escapes that touch the drug. Allosteric and conformational escapes sit far from the ligand and are ranked low by construction.
A co-crystal structure is one conformation of one construct. Residues in disordered loops are absent from the coordinates and cannot be ranked; they are reported, not counted as misses.
7 drug-target pairs and 14 labelled escapes is a small benchmark, and all of them are kinase or BCL2-family inhibitors.
Escape labels are curated from the cited literature, so the benchmark covers escapes that were published, which favours well-studied resistance mechanisms.

recall@10 is sensitive to k here: two contact-mediated escapes (EGFR T790M, ALK L1196M) rank 11th. The recall curve is reported for k from 5 to 20, and the scoring weights were not adjusted after seeing these ranks.
